clue.text: Plots over certain properties

parts.note: plots of planted ground laid out on top of buildings rather than beside them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' suggests schemes and 'properties' suggests qualities, but read literally these are garden plots sitting over (on top of) houses and blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardens planted on a building's top are plots of ground placed above the property itself.

clue.text: Won't tolerate the maltreatment of sisters

indicators.note: maltreatment means rough handling, so the letters of the following word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to put up with cruelty towards their female siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the maltreatment of' rearranges SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or refuse to accept something, the same as declining to tolerate it.

clue.text: There's no place here for gas

parts.note: O is a zero, nought or nothing
a zone is an area or place

explanation.surface: A complaint that somewhere has no room for gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' as the round figure O; 'There's' and 'here for' only join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, found high in the atmosphere, is a gas.

clue.text: The inexperienced endorse American money

parts.note: green means raw, new to something
to back someone is to support or endorse them

explanation.surface: Novices put their signatures on US dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A US banknote is nicknamed for the green ink on its reverse side.

clue.text: Bring up the right to a hearing aid

parts.note: the ear is the organ that aids hearing

explanation.surface: Someone raises the matter of a person's right to a device that helps them hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing aid' is not a device but the body part that does the hearing; 'Bring up' is a verb, as in raising children.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise or nurture them until grown.

clue.text: Sense people rowing will encompass agreement

indicators.note: encompass means surround, so the rowing crew wraps around the word for agreement

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Somebody senses that the rowers will reach a consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will encompass' signals the container; an eight is a racing boat crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Wrap for a writer over 50

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A garment suitable for an author past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets SHAW above L in this down entry; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a cloth worn draped around the shoulders, a type of covering garment.

clue.text: Apt to examine those in the best condition

parts.note: fit means suitable or apt
to test is to examine

explanation.surface: A suitable way to check who is in top shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the definition is the noun phrase, as in survival of the fittest.
explanation.definitionFit: The fittest are the healthiest, in peak physical shape.

clue.text: Call for help to hold down some swine

indicators.note: to hold here means to contain, so the distress signal grips the word for down

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
under means below or down

explanation.surface: An appeal for assistance to restrain a few pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' signals the container. A sounder is the hunting term for a herd of wild boar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounders are herds of wild boar or pigs, collective groups of hogs.

clue.text: Pottery keeping recently-made article in reserve

indicators.note: in places the new piece and the article within the word for reserve

parts.note: a store is a stock kept in reserve
new means recently made
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Ceramics kept with a freshly made piece in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'keeping' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of fired ceramic ware.

clue.text: On the move towards the stern, wearing glasses

indicators.note: something worn sits on the outside, so the word for the back of a ship goes around the glasses

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for towards the back of a vessel
OO pictures a pair of round spectacle lenses

explanation.surface: A sailor heads aft while wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts OO inside AFT. OO for glasses is a visual convention: two round lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is in progress or under way.

clue.text: Considering viewing

explanation.definitionFit: First sense: 'seeing that' means given or considering; second sense: watching or looking at something with the eyes.

clue.text: Once evil characters go berserk there'll be outrage

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words run wild and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Once wicked people run amok there will be public fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters go berserk' rearranges ONCE EVIL; 'there'll be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is an act of brutal force or cruelty, a sense of the word as a violent deed.

clue.text: Quiet about being involved in depressing broadcast

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the quiet and about pieces go inside the word for depressing

parts.note: sad means gloomy or depressing
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A muted remark about being caught up in a gloomy programme on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved in' signals the container. 'broadcast' is the verb in its past form, as in seeds broadcast far and wide.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread something is to scatter or disseminate it widely, as seed or news is broadcast.

clue.text: Only a little of any cereal is edible, that's understood

indicators.note: only a small stretch of the words is taken, the answer lying within them

explanation.surface: Only a small amount of any breakfast grain is fit to eat, it is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only a little of' signals the letters lying inside 'cereal is edible'; 'any' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To have realised something is to have grasped it or become aware of it.

clue.text: The most reasonable copy in the box

indicators.note: in places the word for copy within the container word

parts.note: a chest is a large box
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: The best-value replica is the one packed in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'reasonable' here means reasonably priced, not sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasonable in price means inexpensive, so the most reasonable item costs the least.

clue.text: Reserve foals one's to break

indicators.note: the words are broken up and reassembled in another order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: Distant behaviour that young horses need to be trained out of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges FOALS and ONES; foals are broken in, which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness is a cool, distant manner, the same as reticence or reserve.

clue.text: Cover for a correspondent

parts.note: not a stand-in journalist but the paper wrapper in which a letter writer sends a letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover for a correspondent' suggests someone deputising for a reporter; it is the paper sleeve a letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter writer seals the message in a paper sleeve before posting it.

clue.text: Reach the top man, being fresh and brisk

parts.note: span means extent or reach
the king is the man at the top of the realm

explanation.surface: Getting to the leader while lively and energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link. 'Spanking' as an adjective means vigorous or brisk, as in a spanking pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking breeze or pace is a lively, vigorous one, and spanking new means very fresh.

clue.text: Excellent over fruit? No, quite the opposite!

parts.note: the clue's closing words turn this word into its opposite, under, which is Latin sub
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A superb verdict on a fruit is promptly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, quite the opposite!' tells you to swap 'over' for under, Latin sub; in this down entry the fruit then sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means supreme or outstandingly fine.

clue.text: There's some point in a pest appearing sweet

indicators.note: in places the compass point within the word for the pest

parts.note: a mouse is a household pest
S, south, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A rodent intruder turns up in the pudding, with a point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside MOUSE; 'There's' and 'appearing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dessert, a sweet course in British usage.

clue.text: Intense radical

explanation.definitionFit: First sense: very great or severe in degree; second sense: holding far-reaching views well beyond the mainstream.

clue.text: Red blind, new but spotted

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A window shade, red and brand new, but marked with spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RED BLIND; 'but' is a link. 'spotted' looks like the past of spot, but it is an adjective meaning marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindled describes an animal coat streaked or flecked with darker patches.

clue.text: Straighten clothing

explanation.definitionFit: First sense: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight; second sense: a garment, or attire in general.

clue.text: Compensation for unsatisfactory little plant

parts.note: off means substandard, as in an off day
a set is a young plant or bulb ready for planting, such as an onion set

explanation.surface: Damages paid for a disappointing small seedling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset is something that balances or counteracts another thing, a counterweight or compensation.

clue.text: OK, has arranged it goes ahead?

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters of the preceding words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether everything is settled and the event will proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals the anagram. 'goes ahead' reads as proceeds, but split it: it goes on a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall, peaked military cap, worn on the soldier's head.

clue.text: The constant desire of small Italian children

parts.note: small asks for the short form: It is an abbreviation of Italian

explanation.surface: Young Italians always want things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals abbreviations; 'of' is a link. Italian vermouth is also called It, as in gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing for something.

clue.text: Woman showing anger with heartless nurse

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A woman shows her temper towards an unfeeling nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves NE, the first and last letters of 'nurse'; 'showing' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, taken from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: Going down at one when all at sixes and sevens

indicators.note: the idiom means in total confusion, so the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Things decline once everything is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sixes and sevens' rearranges AT ONE WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something declining or diminishing, like a moon shrinking after full, is going down.

clue.text: Used to determine the regularity of beatings

definitions.text: Used to determine the regularity of beatings

parts.words: Used to determine the regularity of beatings
parts.note: not about punishment but the doctor's instrument for listening to heartbeats

explanation.walkthrough: 'beatings' suggests punishment; the beats are those of the heart, checked by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's listening instrument is held to the chest to hear the heart's rhythm.
